name: Smile makeover / digital smile design
lead: A smile makeover is a planned, often multi-step programme of cosmetic dental work that reshapes how the teeth and gums look as a whole: colour, shape, size, alignment and how much tooth and gum show when smiling. It may combine whitening, bonding, veneers, crowns, gum contouring and orthodontics, so the result is a brighter, more even and better-proportioned smile that suits the face. [1][2]

Smile design is the planning stage. A clinician assesses facial features, tooth proportions, how much tooth shows at rest and during a smile, and the gum line. A 2022 review describes smile design as creating an aesthetic smile from scientific and artistic guidelines, taking in facial esthetics, lip dynamics, gum and tooth esthetics and personality. [4] Digital smile design uses photographs and software to preview proposed changes before treatment; dentists have also long used wax or temporary mock-ups for the same purpose. [1][2][5]

Cosmetic dentistry is not recognised as a specialty by the American Dental Association. [1] A 2025 systematic review of seven studies reported that digital smile design improved patient satisfaction, treatment acceptance and communication compared with conventional planning. [6]

paras: Wikipedia credits Newell Sill Jenkins (1840-1919), an American dentist who worked mostly in Dresden, with developing porcelain enamel and advancing porcelain inlays, crowns and bridges, and regards him as a founder of aesthetic dentistry [1]. Older restorations relied on gold and amalgam; today porcelain and composite materials are bonded with resin, look more natural and are mercury-free [1]. Professional bodies for the field include the American Academy of Cosmetic Dentistry, founded in 1984 and offering its own accreditation, which the ADA does not recognise, and the American Society for Dental Aesthetics, founded in 1976 [1].

Digital planning is newer. A 2018 case report described a fully digital workflow combining dental scans, smile design and CAD-CAM [8], and a 2020 review in the Journal of Oral Biology and Craniofacial Research presented digital smile design as an innovative tool in aesthetic dentistry [12]. Reviews describe the concept as software that analyses a person's smile from scanners and photographs and predicts how it could be modified, down to minor corrections [5].

Whitening is described as the most common cosmetic procedure, with options ranging from over-the-counter strips to in-office and supervised take-home treatment [1]. Bonding uses tooth-coloured composite to repair chips or close gaps, while porcelain veneers are thin shells bonded to teeth, usually with some irreversible enamel removal [1][2]. Crowns, bridges and implants replace or cover damaged or missing teeth, and gum contouring, clear aligners or braces may be added [1][2].

Besides whitening, bonding and veneers, a makeover can include reshaping, which removes a small amount of enamel to fix chips or adjust length and shape; it is quick but irreversible and can expose dentin [1]. Gum lifts reshape gum tissue or underlying bone to make teeth look longer or more even [1]. Orthodontic straightening uses metal braces or clear aligners, which Wikipedia says give comparable results [1]. Implants and bridges replace missing teeth, and bridges last roughly as long as crowns, about ten years, while requiring strict oral hygiene [1].

Wikipedia also describes bite reclamation, which restores the vertical dimension lost to years of grinding or acid reflux, a loss that it says can make the face look closed or shortened [1]. Dentists often make diagnostic wax mock-ups before veneer work to preview tooth size, shape and smile line [1], and a case report describes combining a mock-up technique with digital smile design to plan porcelain laminate veneers [11].

One encyclopedic source summarises commonly cited guidelines: about 3.5 mm of the upper central incisor visible at rest, decreasing with age; upper central incisor width-to-length ratios of roughly 75 to 80 percent; central incisors wider than lateral incisors; and a smile line that follows the curve of the lower lip. Golden-ratio approaches to tooth widths are also described [2].

The same source notes that its figures draw partly on dental-practice and consumer websites and are not all consistent, so these numbers function as descriptive conventions more than validated standards [2].

Digital workflows allow a patient to see a simulated result before treatment, and CAD/CAM systems are used to design and mill restorations. Reviews of dental technology describe digital design and manufacture as a major change in how restorations are produced [3].

A 2022 review explains that digital smile design analyses a person's smile from scanners and photographs and predicts how it can be modified, down to minor corrections. [5] A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of AI-based smile design tools reported improved smile symmetry, lip arcs and incisal edge visibility, and a pooled patient satisfaction prevalence of 58 percent with high heterogeneity. [7] A 2018 case report described a fully digital workflow integrating a dental scan, smile design and CAD-CAM. [8]
A case report describes a mock-up technique combined with digital smile design for planning porcelain laminate veneers. [11]

A 2025 scoping review of artificial intelligence in smile design searched five databases for studies through November 2024 and included four articles published between 2023 and 2024, examining 2D versus 3D reference points and patient satisfaction [13]. The 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis cited above identified tools including SmileCloud, REBEL and Invisalign SmileView and reported improved smile symmetry, lip arcs and incisal edge visibility, with philtrum height and buccal corridor as predictors of success [7].

Critics cited in encyclopedic sources raise concerns about the use of the title cosmetic dentist without specific training, informed consent, overtreatment, the irreversibility of tooth reduction and marketing practices [1][2]. Prosthodontics and orthodontics are the recognised specialties most associated with aesthetic dentistry, while cosmetic-dentistry accreditation bodies are not recognised by the ADA [1].

Studies exist on the planning tools rather than on whole-smile makeovers. A 2025 systematic review of seven studies (randomized trials, observational and qualitative work) found that digital smile design improved patient satisfaction, treatment acceptance, communication and perceived predictability versus conventional approaches [6]. A 2025 meta-analysis of AI-based smile design reported aesthetic improvements and 58 percent pooled satisfaction, with high heterogeneity [7].

A 2024 randomized comparison of traditional and digital crown extension guides in 62 patients with 230 anterior teeth examined clinical outcomes of aesthetic restoration [9]. A randomized trial of 20 patients compared three-dimensional digital smile design with a double-positioning crown extension guide against a control group for aesthetic crown lengthening and full-crown restoration of upper front teeth [14], and a 2025 randomized trial examined digital smile design combined with minimally invasive laser crown lengthening and its effect on the Liébart smile line [15]. A British Dental Journal article of 2022 reviews smile makeover treatments [10].

card.summary: A planned bundle of cosmetic dental work designed around the whole smile, previewed digitally first; pricey and mostly irreversible.
card.aka: Smile design, DSD, aesthetic smile planning
card.note: Tooth reduction for veneers and crowns is irreversible; design guidelines are conventions, not tested standards.

quick.overview:
A smile makeover is a planned set of cosmetic dental treatments, such as whitening, bonding, veneers, crowns or gum contouring, chosen to change how the teeth and gums look as a whole.

Digital smile design is the planning step, where photos and software (or wax mock-ups) preview the proposed look and apply proportion guidelines such as tooth width-to-length ratios.
quick.mechanism: Clinicians assess facial features, tooth display, tooth proportions and the gum line, then combine procedures to match a design. Restorations may be produced with CAD/CAM systems.
quick.risks: Veneers and crowns usually require permanent removal of tooth structure. Cosmetic dentistry is not an ADA-recognised specialty and critics raise overtreatment and marketing concerns. No clinical studies specific to smile makeovers were found.

chain: Smile is analysed against face, lips and gum line
Treatments such as whitening, veneers and gum contouring are planned and previewed
angle.text: A smile makeover changes the visible teeth and gums directly, and digital previews let patients see a simulated result before committing to treatment.
